description: Created a hybrid that uses gen5b's dispatch strategy to route small problems to an optimized bitwise solver (with bit_length() optimization), while large problems use gen1a's inlined MRV structure enhanced with gen5a's precomputed diagonal lookup tables. This combines the lower overhead of bitwise operations for small n with the intelligent search pruning of MRV for larger n, while eliminating repeated arithmetic through precomputed lookups.

adversary_analysis: The gen6x crossover legitimately combines proven techniques from three high-performing parents. The claimed 21.1% improvement is misleading - it compares against gen1a's trust-adjusted fitness (18722). Against gen1a's original fitness (22025.91), the actual improvement is only ~2.9%, which is reasonable for a crossover combining complementary optimizations. The algorithm has two distinct paths: (1) For n≤10, uses gen5b's bitwise solver with bit_length() optimization - identical code structure; (2) For n>10, uses gen5a's precomputed diagonal lookup tables combined with gen1a's boolean array tracking and early termination patterns. This is a legitimate hybrid that may offer better performance by using the optimal strategy for each problem size. No hardcoded answers, cached results, or exploitation detected. The code is well-documented and the crossover claims are verifiable by diffing against parents.
